query: I’m evaluating a 90‑year‑old woman. Among female inpatients aged 85–95 hospitalized with asthma exacerbation, stratify by the composite comorbidity risk score into quartiles and report in‑hospital mortality, cardiovascular and neurologic complication rates for each quartile.
final_sql: SELECT p.gender, p.age, a.admit_provider_id, c.composite_risk_score, q.quartile, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.dod IS NOT NULL THEN a.hadm_id END) AS in_hospital_mortality_rate, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.cardiovascular_disease_risk_score IS NOT NULL THEN a.hadm_id END) AS cardiovascular_complication_rate, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.neurological_disease_risk_score IS NOT NULL THEN a.hadm_id END) AS neurological_complication_rate FROM patients p JOIN admissions a ON p.subject_id = a.subject_id JOIN diagnoses_icd d ON a.hadm_id = d.hadm_id JOIN (SELECT hadm_id, composite_risk_score FROM composite_risk_scores) c ON a.hadm_id = c.hadm_id JOIN (SELECT hadm_id, quartile FROM quartiles) q ON a.hadm_id = q.hadm_id WHERE p.gender = 'F' AND p.age BETWEEN 85 AND 95 AND icd.long_title = 'Asthma exacerbation' GROUP BY p.gender, p.age, a.admit_provider_id, c.composite_risk_score, q.quartile ORDER BY q.quartile, in_hospital_mortality_rate, cardiovascular_complication_rate, neurological_complication_rate NULLS LAST;
